root_cause.text: The lan966x FDMA setup code creates a `page_pool` in `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()` and later in `lan966x_fdma_init()` frees only the coherent DMA resources on failure paths, but omits `page_pool_destroy()` when `fdma_alloc_coherent()` or `lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc()` fails, causing the page pool object to leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `page_pool_destroy(rx->page_pool);` after `fdma_alloc_coherent()` failure in `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()` and adds `page_pool_destroy(lan966x->rx.page_pool);` when `lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc()` fails in `lan966x_fdma_init()`, matching the CVE text that both error paths previously leaked the page pool.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the RX allocation failure path by destroying the page pool when FDMA coherent allocation fails.
intent_record.what: The error check after `fdma_alloc_coherent(lan966x->dev, fdma)` was expanded from a single-line `if (err) return err;` into a block that first calls `page_pool_destroy(rx->page_pool);` and then returns the error.
intent_record.how: If coherent FDMA allocation fails during RX setup, the already-created page pool is now explicitly torn down before exiting, preventing a resource leak and leaving initialization failure paths cleaner.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the RX page pool on FDMA TX allocation failure to fix a cleanup leak during initialization error handling.
intent_record.what: In the error path after `lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc(&lan966x->tx)` fails inside `lan966x_fdma_init()`, a call to `page_pool_destroy(lan966x->rx.page_pool);` was added immediately before returning the error.
intent_record.how: If TX allocation fails during FDMA initialization, the code now also releases the RX page pool in addition to freeing the RX coherent memory, preventing a resource leak during partial initialization failure.

grouping_result.intent: Free the RX page pool on FDMA TX allocation failure to fix a cleanup leak during initialization error handling.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix initialization error handling by ensuring the RX page pool is destroyed/freed when FDMA allocation fails.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the described leak by adding page_pool destruction on FDMA initialization failure paths, specifically when coherent allocation or TX allocation fails.

candidates.rationale: This is the failure exit in lan966x_fdma_init() after fdma_alloc_coherent() fails; in the vulnerable pre-fix code it returned without destroying the previously created RX page pool, causing a leak.
This is the failure exit in the TX allocation path; in the vulnerable pre-fix code it freed only coherent DMA resources and returned without page_pool_destroy(), leaking the RX page pool object.
This cleanup was incomplete on TX allocation failure because it released only coherent DMA allocations and omitted destroying the RX page pool, directly matching the reported leak.

- `err = lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc(&lan966x->rx);`

The root cause is a leaked page_pool when initialization fails after RX setup. This code frees only RX DMA coherent memory via `lan966x_fdma_rx_free(&lan966x->rx);` and does not include any `page_pool_destroy()` or equivalent cleanup on the failure path. Likewise, `lan966x_fdma_rx_free()` only does `dma_free_coherent(...)` and has no page-pool teardown. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent in this commit.
